parsedVerdict.reasoning: The module passes. All six files are application use-case classes for one task-management domain (projects, tasks, users), and they share the same shape: dependencies passed in through the constructor, one async execute(input) method, and a DTO returned through the matching to*Dto mapper. Every file uses the module's abstractions consistently. Persistence always goes through the repository interfaces (TaskRepository, ProjectRepository, UserRepository). Ids always come from IdGenerator. Business rules stay in domain entities, value objects and services (Task.create, task.markDone, TaskAssignmentService.assign, TaskTitle, DueDate, TaskStatus.from). No file reimplements a domain invariant or skips past an abstraction. The look-up-then-throw-NotFoundError lines are repeated in four files, but this is ordinary use-case boilerplate rather than a duplicated business rule, because the error type itself is defined once in the domain. Likewise, the optional TaskStatus.from conversion appears in two files, but both hand the rule to the same value object instead of copying its logic.
